taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kogam-street, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 127 | 0.822 | 0.822
2 | 50.4 | 5.63 | 6.45
3 | 126 | 21.2 | 27.7
4 | 149 | 29.7 | 57.3
5 | 197 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kogam-street, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station Kogam-street, Bori Metropolis. The subsurface profile consists of five layers with resistivity values of 127, 50.4, 126, 149, and 197 ohm-m. The thicknesses for the first four layers are 0.822m, 5.63m, 21.2m, and 29.7m, respectively. Based on the resistivity transitions, the sequence follows an H-A-A pattern: the first three layers show a decrease then increase (H), while the subsequent transitions (2-3-4 and 3-4-5) show continuous increases (A). This matches the HAA curve-type classification currently noted on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "HAA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
